quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. These warn you and show you where to go.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system in your vehicle is dangerous because it can cause:

options.text: A loss of hearing.
Pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes exhaust gas and keeps fumes out of the passenger area. A leak can allow poisonous gas to enter your car. Fix leaks right away to stay safe.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down, move it completely off the road if you can. All four wheels should be off the main driving surface.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about driving on a wet roadway?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you decrease your speed, the roadway becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
questions.explanation: When driving fast on wet roads, your tires cannot push water away. At very high speeds, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane—your car slides on a layer of water.

questions.question: A person who drives much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be dangerous. If traffic backs up behind you on a two-lane road, you must pull over and let cars pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: Another driver is trying to pass your car. You should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when someone passes you. Look for oncoming cars and slow down a little to help them pass safely.

questions.question: Two solid white lines painted across a traffic lane show the boundaries of a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians are responsible to stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines mark where pedestrians should cross safely. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, you should:

options.text: Decrease your speed.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
Use your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be dangerous. If traffic backs up behind you on a two-lane road, you must pull over and let cars pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip the road better than when you are driving on pavement.
Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads offer less grip than paved roads. Slow down on these surfaces. Your car will take longer to stop and is more likely to skid when turning.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision at an intersection. No one is hurt and there is little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
Not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of traffic if you safely can.

questions.question: When you see this sign, what should you do?

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
Merge right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Do not stop on the shoulder unless there is an emergency. Avoid changing lanes often. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull all the way off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the pavement, stay calm. Take your foot off the accelerator and slow down. Keep both hands on the wheel and steer gently back onto the road. Check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: It is unlawful to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle. Motorcyclists need the full lane width to maneuver safely.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit.
questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not back up, stop, or make a U-turn on the highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when changing lanes, pulling into traffic, or moving into a parking space.

questions.question: If you drive slower than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:

options.text: Interfere with traffic and get a ticket.
Improve traffic flow.
Demonstrate defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Interfere with traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you block the normal flow of traffic, you may get a ticket. Match the speed of traffic unless the traffic speed exceeds the legal limit.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: When the train has passed.
Under no circumstances.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, flaggers, or train horns. Never drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: When passing another car, you have enough space to return to the driving lane:

options.text: If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.
If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
If you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure there is a safe distance between your car and the passed car before returning to the lane. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return.

questions.question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rainy or foggy weather. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they do not help you see much better.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?

options.text: School zone ahead.
Yield to other traffic.
Construction zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. You must slow down and let other traffic pass. Once the road is clear and safe, you can proceed.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is correct?

options.text: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both driving too slowly on some highways and speeding can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both driving too slowly on some highways and speeding can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the risk of death increases. At speeds above 80 mph, you have almost no chance of surviving a crash. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may become impatient and make unsafe moves to pass you.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
Slow down and use high beam headlights.
Turn lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If you cannot see the road, pull over and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to prevent accidents.
Passing bad drivers by speeding ahead of them.
Following the car in front of you closely.
Quickly changing lanes to get around traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. This helps you avoid crashes with unsafe, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When used on roadways, bicycles are considered what?

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles when used on roadways. Bicycle riders and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Traffic merging from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions just ahead. This sign tells you to be ready for traffic to merge safely from the right.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Use your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to create more distance.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors several times a minute to notice tailgaters, speeding cars, or cars trying to pass. If someone is following you too closely, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because one car is following too closely.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, make sure no vehicles are in the space you want to enter. Check your mirrors and blind spots by looking over your shoulder. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes to give other drivers time to react.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is beginning.
You may see pedestrians.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the posted times. An "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror on each side eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
You can see blind spots by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have larger blind spots. Other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians crossing against the traffic light.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Pedestrians may cross against the light by mistake, so always be ready to stop for them.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.
Lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection is ahead.

questions.question: To enter a freeway:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of other vehicles.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly to check traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Signal before merging and match the speed of traffic. Always yield to other vehicles already on the freeway.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your low beam headlights.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.
